newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 2.00 to 3.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 2.00 to 3.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open down 2.00 to 3.00 cents Tuesday as traders expect a technical correction to Monday's sharp run-up.

However, some traders said prices were likely to come in closer to unchanged. "It's called lower, but I think it will come in unchanged," one floor trader said. "I just don't see any sellers out here."

Monday, the New York arabica market vaulted to new contract highs, boosted by speculative buying and trade shortcovering. July futures finished up 11.75 cents at 229.65 cents a lb after trading from a new lifetime high of 230.25 cents to 218.70 cents. Spot May rose 6.65 cents to 245.65 cents, while the back months closed 4.35 to 8.90 higher.
The July/September switch ballooned to 225.20 cents compared with 22.35 cents at the close on Friday.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks increased by 4,373 bags, to 31,292 bags as of May 9. There were 28,620 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures surged to one-year highs early Tuesday, but eased off peaks by midday. LIFFE July was up $40 at the break, to $1,815, after ranging from $1,835 to $1,800.
